items.title: The first cultured meat burger
items.claim: The first publicly cooked and tasted cultured meat burger was presented in London in 2013. Roughly what did it cost to produce?
items.reveal_title: About a third of a million dollars per burger
items.reveal:
Mark Post's 5 August 2013 demonstration used cultured bovine muscle cells. The project was funded by Sergey Brin.

By 2023 Singapore and the US approved limited cultured chicken sales; production costs remain orders of magnitude above conventional meat.
items.why: Technologies start at extreme costs that fall steeply if scale is achieved.

items.title: What Pasteur first pasteurised
items.claim: Louis Pasteur developed pasteurisation in the 1860s. What was he originally trying to preserve?
items.reveal_title: Pasteurisation began with wine, not milk
items.reveal:
Pasteur's 1866 work Etudes sur le vin addressed spoilage in French wines. He showed heating to about 50-60 C killed the microbes that caused spoilage without ruining flavour.

Milk pasteurisation became widespread later, accelerated by urban infant mortality concerns from the 1890s.
items.why: Technologies often arrive in industries far from where they were originally invented.

items.title: Industrial trans fats banned
items.claim: Industrial trans fats from partial hydrogenation were once common in margarine and processed food. Denmark was first to set strict national limits. In which year?
items.reveal_title: Denmark restricted industrial trans fats in 2003
items.reveal:
The US FDA effectively eliminated artificial trans fats by 2018. WHO's REPLACE programme set global elimination targets.

Mortality modelling estimated tens of thousands of cardiovascular deaths prevented in Denmark alone.
items.why: Public-health regulation can change food formulations across an entire economy.
